u0: Initial carrying phase: the agent starts with the box in hand before the first fall and should head toward the exit while keeping it. If the box falls, begin recovery; if the exit is reached while still holding it, the task succeeds.
u1: Immediate recovery after the first fall: the box has just slipped away and the agent is empty-handed. Pick it up on the very next step; doing so before the exit advances to the post-recovery carrying phase with partial progress, while failing to regain it immediately leads to failure. Reaching the exit already holding the recovered box also completes the task.
u2: Post-first-fall carrying phase: the agent has picked the box back up on the required next move and is carrying it again toward the exit. If another scheduled fall occurs, switch immediately to recovery again; otherwise continue to the exit and finish with the box in hand.
u3: Immediate recovery after a second fall: the box has just fallen again and the agent is empty-handed. Pick it up on the very next step; successful recovery moves into the final carrying phase with partial progress, whereas failing to regain it immediately is a terminal failure for reward. Reaching the exit while already holding it also completes the task.
u4: Final carrying phase: the agent has recovered from the second fall and holds the box again; no further recovery stage remains. Continue to the exit and arrive while still holding the box to complete the task.
u5: Failure sink: after a fall, the agent did not pick the box up on the very next step, so the reward machine can no longer reach the success state. The episode may continue, but no final reward is available.
u6: Success terminal: the agent reached the exit while holding the box. The task is complete, the final reward is collected, and no further objective remains.
